figures.caption: Schematic workflow of AMPidentifier tool. The gut microbiome data were utilized to discover potential AMP candidates, leading to candidate AMPs for chemical synthesis and laboratory testing. A Advanced deep learning models were employed to distinguish AMPs from non-AMPs, using various features such as physical, chemical, sequence, and structural data as model inputs. B Methods for discovering AMPs from gut microbiome data sourced from the pathogenic insect B. germanica
figures.label: Fig. 1

figures.caption: Mining potential AMPs from the gut microbiome of B. germanica. A The AI deep learning model predicted potential AMP sequences from various developmental stages of B. germanica’s gut microbiome. These samples were classified as oot, n1, n2, n3, n4, and n5, corresponding to embryos and individuals on days 2, 11, 15, 22, and 34 after hatching, respectively. B, C, D Comparative analysis of physiochemical properties including isoelectric points, aromaticity, molecular weight, hydrophobicity, charge at pH 7.0, and secondary structure compositions (α-helix, β-structure, and others) between known AMPs (KA) and AI-predicted AMPs (PA). E AI scores and occurrence rates of 79 potential AMPs identified in B. germanica. F Selection criteria for AMP used in experimental validation
figures.label: Fig. 2

figures.caption: Experiments verify the potencies of functional AMPs. A Experimental pipeline for rapid cell-free biosynthesis of the predicted AMPs from synthetic DNA fragments and direct testing of produced AMPs in the cell-free mix to bacterial cultures followed by propidium iodide (PI) fluorescence detection assay. B Circular dichroism (CD) spectra of AMP1 and predicted atomic structure of AMP1 by AlphaFold 3.0. AMP1 was in deionized water, and the concentration of AMP1 was fixed at 0.1 mg/mL. C Antibacterial activities of AMP1 towards different bacteria. PC, positive control. In the evaluation of the antimicrobial activity of AMPs against B. subtilis 23,857, E. coli 25,404, and S. aureus 6538, the positive control was represented by 100-μM kanamycin. In the assessment of AMPs against P. aeruginosa 27,853, the positive control was represented by 100-μM ampicillin. D Detection of cytotoxicity of AMP1. The representative optical microscopy images of C2C12 cells are shown here, with a scale bar = 200 µm
figures.label: Fig. 3

figures.caption: Action mechanisms of AMP1. A Representative images obtained from confocal laser scanning microscopy to analyze the behavior of AMP1. B. subtilis cells were treated with coumarin 343-labeled AMP1 at a concentration of 100 μM for various durations before observation. During observation, the B. subtilis cells membrane was stained with FM4-64. The scale bar on the left represents 10 μm, while the magnified view provides a scale bar of 2 μm. B Representative confocal laser scanning microscopy image showing dead cell staining after treatment with AMP1 at a concentration of 100 μM for 1 min. The scale bar represents 10 μm. C The quantification of cell membrane potential revealed by DiSC3(5) fluorescence. Triton-X100 (final concentration 0.2%) was the positive control. D Representative confocal laser scanning microscopy images of dead cells stained with PI at various time points following treatment with AMP1 at a concentration of 100 μM. The scale bar represents 10 μm. E Representative confocal laser scanning microscopy image of B. subtilis cells treated with AMP1 at a concentration of 100 μM for 6 h. DNA was stained using DAPI. The scale bar represents 10 μm. F The SEM examination of B. subtilis cells treated with AMPs at concentrations of 100 μM showed cell content leakage and disruption of cell wall. All ruptured cells were indicated by a purple arrow. The scale bar represents 2 μm. G Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations calculating AMP1 with bacterial-mimicking POPE/POPG (2:1) membranes or mammalian POPC membranes
figures.label: Fig. 4

figures.caption: Action mechanisms of AMP1-2L. A Comparative analysis of AMP1 and AMP1-2L sequences and AlphaFold 3.0 predicted structures. The blue and green regions of the sequence correspond to sequences that form β-strands, respectively. Gray areas correspond to sequences forming other secondary structures. Trp and Leu are highlighted in orange boxes. B Comparative analysis of CD spectra and structural composition of AMP1 and AMP1-2L at a concentration of 0.1 mg/mL. C Representative images obtained from confocal laser scanning microscopy to analyze the behavior of AMP1-2L. B. subtilis cells were treated with coumarin 343-labeled AMP1-2L at a concentration of 100 μM for various durations before observation. During observation, the B. subtilis cells membrane was stained with FM4-64. The scale bar on the left represents 10 μm, while the magnified view provides a scale bar of 2 μm. D The predicted half-life time for AMP1 and AMP1-2L. The inset illustrates the hydrophobicity scores of AMP1 and AMP1-2L, with GRAVY (grand average of hydrophobicity) indicating positive values for hydrophobicity. E MD simulations calculating AMP1-2L with bacterial-mimicking POPE/POPG (2:1) membranes. F MD simulations calculating AMP1 and AMP1-2L in aqueous environments with results of RMSD and RMSF for assessing the structural stability
figures.label: Fig. 5

figures.caption: The wound healing in vivo therapeutic assessments of AMP1. A Representative wound healing results in an infected mouse model treated with control PBS, AMP1, and vancomycin at the same dosage in vivo. B Experimental verification of S. aureus infection load in control, AMP1-treated, and vancomycin-treated groups by streaking on LB agar plates. C Representative histological images of infected tissues from control, AMP1-treated, and vancomycin-treated groups, generated using H&E and Masson staining methods. D Representative histological images selected from repeated experiments for indicating α-SMA, CD31, and FGF2 levels of the AMP1 treatment group and control group at days 1 and 12. The statistical analysis of biomarkers α-SMA, CD31, and FGF2 indicator levels is calculated by ImageJ software among control, AMP1-treated, and vancomycin-treated groups at days 12 with 3 sampling replicates in each group. The scale bar represents 100 μm. The overall significance was assessed by t-test (p* ≤ 0.05, p** ≤ 0.01, p*** ≤ 0.001)
